subject: Fraud & Scams
title: The Tulip Mania Bubble
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Tulip Mania Bubble.

hook.text: In 1637, a single tulip bulb sold for more than a canal house in Amsterdam.

buildup.text: Dutch traders bid up rare tulip varieties, creating a speculative frenzy.

discovery.text: Many traders sold bulbs they didn't own, promising future delivery at sky-high prices.

twist.text: When prices crashed overnight, buyers refused to pay. Fortunes vanished in days.

climax.text: Tulip mania became the textbook example of a speculative bubble driven by hype.

punchline.text: A flower worth more than a house is always a scam.
